utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Mettraux, one hour and five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Further cross-examination by Mr. Mettraux:

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will recall that yesterday I asked you a number of questions and I've shown you a number of documents about the involvement of the President of the Republic of Macedonia in the events of Ljuboten; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have that information at the time of writing your report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you make any inquiry with the commander of the local army battalion in the area of Ljuboten to obtain information from them?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiry with the commander of the brigade of the army which was present in the area of Ljuboten at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiry with the General Staff of the Republic of Macedonia Army?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you a question two days ago in relation to your contacts with members of the Office of the Prosecutor. I would also like to ask you whether, during the preparation of your report, the Ljuboten report, you had any contact with Mr. Frederick Abrahams.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall having communicated with Mr. Abrahams while you were in Macedonia, at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams accompanied me for several of my trips to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, I was -- meant to ask about your fourth trip, the trip that you took from the 17th to the 25th or 26th of August. Did you have any phone contacts with Mr. Abrahams during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Abrahams assist you in relation to the editing of the report on Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct that on the 25th of August, or prior to that time, you communicated the content of your findings to a journalist, Ms. Jessica Berry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct. We had a conversation about the contents of the report, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that correct that at that time, the -- your report or the content of that report had not yet been vetted by your colleagues and superior in New York?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was in the process of being vetted, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And am I correct also to understand that it was your position, at the time of preparing your report and in your conclusions, you took the view that the victims of the incidents had all been civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: As I -- that was our opinion based on the evidence available to us. But as our report makes clear, even if there had been an NLA presence in Ljuboten, the attacks that we documented were deliberate attacks against civilians or indiscriminate attacks against civilians or civilian property, so they would still have been violations of the laws of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct that you made that assessment without seeing any of the dead bodies, aside from the body of Mr. Qaili; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had extensive photographic evidence of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct that you made that finding without any forensic evidence, is that correct, which related to the deceased, that is?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had photographs, the detailed photographs which were available to us, as well as the field notes of Mr. -- the journalist Nicholas Wood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take your answer as, no, you did not have any forensic material. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had information about the wounds on the victims from both the photographs and the field notes of Mr. Nicholas Wood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that correct that in your experience both in Kosovo and in Macedonia, you would be aware of the fact that members of the UCK would not always wear their uniforms and that they would sometimes wear a mixture of civilian and military clothing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: In my experience in Macedonia, whenever I interacted with the UCK, the NLA, they were in uniforms. But I am aware of reports where they were seen -- some members were seen out of uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would agree that there were times when, indeed, the NLA would mix with the civilian population; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: In or out of uniform?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Out of uniform.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had no personal incidents in which I saw the UCK mix with the civilian population out of uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct that in the first statement which you gave to the Prosecution, you indicated that one way in which you made the determination that an individual or a deceased had been a civilian or not was by looking at the shoes which this person was wearing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was a relevant factor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to show this witness a number of pictures. The first picture would be Rule 65 ter 2D00236.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated to the Prosecution that members of the NLA, in your understanding, would generally wear military boots; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can focus simply on the gentleman on the right-hand side of the picture. Would you agree that, at least as far as you can tell from this picture, this person on the right would appear to be a combatant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have no information about what this picture represents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in your view, would this person be a legitimate target should he take any part in military activities?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: If he was out -- yes, but it's quite common for people in the Balkans, of all ethnicities, to pose with weapons. It doesn't necessarily mean that this person is a UCK combatant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct, however, that this person is wearing sneakers?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we see what is Rule 65 ter 2D00250.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, are you able, from this picture, to say whether any of these individuals is a combatant, and if so, which one? Would you be able to make that assessment?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Again, I have no information about what this picture represents, but there are a number of people with weapons in the picture. And if this was in a situation of conflict, they could be legitimately targeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you be able to state from that picture which one would be considered legitimate combatants, legitimate targets and combatants?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the picture isn't very clear, so it's a little bit difficult to tell who exactly is carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps by --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: But even by mixing with combatants, these civilians would be placing themselves at risk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, with the assistance of the usher, Mr. Bouckaert, I'll ask you to do -- to mark something on the picture. If you could encircle the first individual on the left side of the picture, the man with longish hair and what would appear to be a beard, if you could simply circle him.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could place the number "1" above that circle.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could do the same exercise in relation to the third individual from the left with the number "2".

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could do it again, please, with the man who has a -- the third -- the fourth man who has a hand up, the man with a beard and a white T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we tender this picture?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For what purpose?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the purpose will become clear in the next picture, Your Honour. I can identify this picture to solve the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 2D00249.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D93 -- 1D93, MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recognise, sir, the individuals whom you marked as number 1, 2, and 3 in this picture?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: They certainly look similar, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree that the second person from the right-hand corner of that picture, the man with longish hair and a beard, would be number 1?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps what we can do, with the assistance of the Registry, is it possible to put the two pictures, this one and the previous one, side by side on the screen? Thank you. Well, Mr. Bouckaert, are you now able to see the picture -- both pictures at the same time. Would you agree that the person which you marked as number 1 on the extreme left of the picture, on the left, is the same as the second man on the second picture second from the right?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that the third person on the picture on the left is the same as the first picture on the right from the right of the picture?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree that the fourth man from the left on the picture on the left is the same as the first man from the left on the right picture?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we wish to tender these two pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there has been no link established between the gentlemen -- the four gentlemen in the photograph on the right and the events in the village of Ljuboten in August of 2001. We don't know where this picture was taken, nor do we know when it was taken. And the same goes, frankly, with now the photograph on the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply, Your Honour, the issue -- there is no suggestion on our part that any of these individuals was in Ljuboten on -- Ljuboten. They clearly are members of the NLA. The issue is one which Mr. Bouckaert has touched upon both in his report and in his evidence to the Prosecution as to the status of civilians and/or combatants and the ability of anyone, be it an investigator, a member of the army, or anyone else, for that matter, including the Chamber, to be able to make an assessment as to the status of particular victims, in particular the question of whether the clothing of a particular individual would be evidence relevant in or in any case sufficient to establish the status of the alleged victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my learned colleague says that these four individuals are clearly members of the NLA. That clarity, Your Honour, is not obvious to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The last photograph will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be 1D94, MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Neither of them at the moment are shown to have relevance sufficient to be an exhibit, and we will evaluate whether that situation changes in light of other evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, is that correct that you did not search any of the bodies in Ljuboten at the time? You arrived after the bodies had been buried; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever become aware that one of the five dead bodies of the village had 26 rounds of live ammunition in his pockets?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- were you in possession at the time of writing your report of any sort of ballistic report which you used for the purpose of preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask you to slow down and make pauses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We've been warned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yet again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, I think I heard your response, but if you were able to state it again.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, the answer to your question was "no."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware at the time that three guns and ammunition had been found close to the three bodies which were located close-by the Jashari house; were you aware of that fact at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not aware of that fact, and I am not aware of any public statement by the Macedonian authorities, which would have been the usual course of action, making the public aware of that fact and the media aware of that fact. And I would find it quite strange, given the fact that Mr. Boskoski had commented on the events in Ljuboten, that he didn't mention this, considering the international attention on the Ljuboten events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer to the question is: You were not in possession of this information and did not come into possession of this information until a later time; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that also correct that upon the signing of the Orhid Framework Agreement, I believe, on the 13th of August of 2001, discussion were already taking place about the possibility of adopting an amnesty law, is that correct, for crimes committed during the crisis in 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that also correct that the draft of that law was being prepared in the course of the year 2001; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall also that at several stages during the last few months of the year of 2001, the President of the Republic, Boris Trajkovski, made several announcements about this amnesty and undertook to amnesty a number of crimes committed in the crisis?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct, also, and I think you I had shown you the letter yesterday, that Human Rights Watch took a position in relation to that law on the 2nd of October of 2001, addressing the matter with the President and suggesting your concern about this particular amnesty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It's the general position of Human Rights Watch in all conflicts that there should be no amnesties for violations of the laws of war, crimes against humanity and genocide.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct also that you expressed this concern again in the year of 2002, when the completion of the preparation for the law were nearing their end?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that also correct that it was your understanding, at the time that the amnesty law would apply to both sides of the crisis, that would be members of the NLA and members of forces of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, and we expressed concern about cases on both sides that should not be included in the amnesty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct that you also expressed particular concerns about the violence which you had recorded in your Ljuboten incident; is that correct that you specified this particular incident in particular?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think we talked about crimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did; thank you. Is that correct also that despite the protestations or the concern, I should say, of your organisation, the law was eventually adopted in the early months of 2002?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe so. As I made clear yesterday, by that time I was in Afghanistan and Pakistan, following a different war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, we discussed a particular matter, if you recall, about the status of the NLA, and in particular I asked you a number of questions about the position of the United States as regard the NLA. And I would read back to you this very short exchange. I asked you this: "But is that correct that the NLA was regarded by the United States, by the government of the United States, as a terrorist organisation and called as such; is that correct?" And your answer was: "I'm not aware of any statements from the United States describing the NLA as a terrorist organisation, and the NLA was not listed by the United States on its list of terrorists -- terrorist organisations, which does list groups like Hamas and other groups." Do you recall saying this?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is page 3179, Your Honour, the 4th of July, 2007.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I simply want to clarify with you, Mr. Bouckaert, on that point. Is it your position that the United States government did not call the NLA terrorists or extremists, or simply that you are not aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Now you're broadening your question to include the issue of extremism. Your original question was about terrorism.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's start with terrorism, then. Is it your position that the US government did not qualify the NLA as terrorists or is it a situation of not being aware of the fact that they have?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: The -- to the best of my knowledge, the United States never listed the NLA as a terrorist organisation. It has a list of terrorist organisations, and I do not believe that the NLA was on their list at any time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there's a number of statements and information which I would like to show you at this stage. The first one is Rule 65 ter 1D445. It has an ERN of 1D00-4087. Mr. Bouckaert, this is a press article from Agents France press, AFP, dated 12th of April of 2001, and it's an article called "Powell Presses Macedonia Negotiate with Albanians," by the journalist called James Hider [phoen]. And with the Registry's assistance, I would ask that we focus on the bottom of that page. Here, as you can see -- ( Speaking foreign language)

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask you the question. I will kindly ask you to focus on the second paragraph of that article. There's a comment which is attributed to Colin Powell, then Secretary of State of the United States, where he says: "Powell warned that the conflict is over for the moment, but the danger is still there. There are still terrorist and extremist elements working to make trouble in this country." Were you aware of that statement, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not of this particular statement. I don't think it was the general position of the United States government to classify the NLA as terrorists, and neither -- Mr. Powell doesn't mention the NLA in this quote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is that correct that Mr. Powell is a representative of the Government of the United States?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am a representative of Human Rights Watch. In our opinion, the NLA was not a terrorist organisation. It carried out most of its attacks against military objectives, including the attack that took place just before the Ljuboten attack, including the attack on the main Skopje-Tetovo highway, which claimed the lives of ten Macedonian policemen. They did carry out very serious violations, but I do not think that they carried out the kind of terrorist attacks that we saw attempted in London just last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D446, please. It's 1D00-4090.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this is a -- remarks, it's the verbatim, it appears, record of a meeting between Secretary of State, Colin Powell, and the President of the Former Yugoslavic Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski, and it comes from the website of the US State Department, and it relates to a meeting that took place on the 1st of May of 2001. I would ask you to look at the second paragraph of that document. It's a statement taken from Mr. Powell. It says: "And in our meeting today, I once again had the opportunity to express solidarity with Macedonia. The United States' total commitment to territorial integrity of Macedonia, our commitment to this democracy which is facing dastardly and cowardly acts from terrorists and terrorist organisations that are trying to subvert the democratic process in Macedonia. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then if you go two paragraphs further down, it says: "I make the point to the President that we must not allow terrorists to derail political reconciliation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then he goes on to say in the next paragraph: "And I express my condolence and the condolence of the American people to the families of the eight Macedonian soldiers who lost their lives as a result of this terrorist act." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go further down, there's then a passage which is taken from the statement of Mr. Trajkovski, and if you can focus on the third paragraph started with the words: "First of all ...," and particularly the last sentence, Mr. Trajkovski said this: "It shows that the United States would like and is willing to defeat the terrorists, and also to uphold democracy and the rule of law, and also to support the Republic of Macedonia in everything what we are doing." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm sure there are other statements to the same point. But in our legal opinion, an attack carried out against Macedonian soldiers in a remote area, unpopulated area, is not a terrorist attack. It's a very tragic incident, it was a shocking incident for most Macedonians, but under the laws of war it was a legitimate military attack. You know, those NLA members, they could be prosecuted domestically. They don't have the combatants' privilege because it's an internal armed conflict, but we would not classify such an incident as a terrorist incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you focus on the last paragraph on this page, please, and it will go up to the next page in a second. I would like you to look at the second sentence. It says: "I appreciate very ...," and it goes on to the next page: "I appreciate very much that the Secretary stated that we have to isolate the terrorists because they are with one intention, not to encourage the political dialogue, but to destabilise the country, and we have a joint commitment to fight against them with the political sources." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be identified at this stage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be 1D95, MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated, I believe, yesterday and again briefly today, Mr. Bouckaert, that it was your understanding that the NLA contrary to a number of other organisations had not been classified or were not regarded as terrorist organisations, is that correct? And you use, I think, as an opposite example the Hamas?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that the NLA is not listed and was not listed at the time on its list of terrorist organisations, yes. Hamas also wasn't at the time. It is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D448 with an ERN 1D00-416. Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This again is a document entitled "Patterns of Global Terrorism, 2001". It's published by the United States Department of State. It's dated 2002, the month of May, and it relates to the year of 2001. If I could ask the Registry to go to page 53 of that document. It's 1D00-4140. And if the left column of that document could be enlarged. Yes, thank you, and a bit further down, please. Thank you. As you can see, there's a subheading which concerns Israel, the West Bank, and the Gaza Strip, and if we could stroll down a bit further down, please. Then it relates to Hamas conducted several suicide bombings inside Israeli cities from March to June, terminating the attack outside a Tel Aviv nightclub on -- and if we can go on to the next page. It goes on: "1 June that killed 22 Israeli civilians, Israeli teenagers, and injured at least 65 others. On 9 August Hamas mounted a suicide attack in the Jerusalem, its area, killing 50 persons and wounding more than 60 others." Can you see that? ?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can now go to page 31 of that document. That's 1D00-4118. And focus again on the left-hand column -- of the right-hand, I'm sorry, the right side. And if I can draw your attention to the paragraph which starts with the words: "In Southeastern Europe, groups of ethnic Albanians have conducted armed attacks against in southern Serbia forces and Macedonia since 1999. Ethnic Albanian extremists of the so-called National Liberation Army, NLA or UCK, launched an armed insurgency in Macedonia in February. The NLA, which announced its disbandment in July, received funding and weapons not only from Macedonian sources but also from Kosovo and elsewhere. The NLA and a group that operated in Southern Serbia called the Liberation Army of Presevo, Medvedja, and Bujanovac, had strong ties with Kosovar political organisations, including the Popular Movement of Kosovo and the National Movement for the Liberation of Kosovo. Both NLA and UCPMB killed civilians and government security force members and harassed and detained civilians in areas they controlled. Other ethnic Albanian extremist groups also espoused and threatened violence against state institutions in Macedonia and the region, including the so-called Albanian National Army, ANA or AKSH, and the National Committee for the Liberation and Protection of Albanian Lands."

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't see the word "terrorist" mentioned in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we can go back to the first page of the document, please. That's 1D00-4106. And the title of the document is "Pattern of Global Terrorism"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm sure if they meant to classify the NLA as terrorists, they would have mentioned it in the paragraph that you just read.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct that the content of the report concerns patterns of global terrorism?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and it was a descriptive pattern talking about the developments in the Balkans. I didn't see the word "terrorist" mentioned there, and I think it was quite an accurate description of the situation on the ground, both with the UCPMB and UCK in Macedonia and Southern Serbia. I don't have any major disagreements with the description that was given, and it is Human Rights Watch who documented many of those cases of killings of civilians and abuses against civilians by the NLA. I don't think it advances us a lot to try to put the label of terrorism on a group which did not carry out the kind of terrorist actions that Hamas or the IRA or other terrorist groups carry out, or al-Qaeda, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that correct that what you are stating now is the position of your organisation, Human Rights Watch; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We did not use the label "terrorist" to describe the NLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've indicated -- Your Honour, we will leave it as an MFI for the time being. Yesterday, Mr. Bouckaert, you've indicated that -- you've made a few comments about a group sometimes known as The Lions and also referred to sometimes as the Paramilitary 2000. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Before I go any further, Your Honour, I understand the document has not been identified. If I can ask that it be. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be 1D96, MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever sent a request to the Ministry of Interior to obtain information in relation to that particular group?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if evidence was led in this courtroom that the Ministry of Interior in fact investigated that group, you would simply not be in a position to give any evidence on that point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also given evidence on the 2nd of July about an incident which you had reported about in Bitola. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you recalled a number -- I mean, essentially what were riots in that city; can you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, riots involving some elements of the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to that particular incident, did you make any request to the Ministry of Interior for information pertaining to that incident?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters need to ask you again to slow down and make pauses, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply for the record, the reference in page 21, line 15, it refers to the 2nd of July. The date of the 2nd of July was the date at which Mr. Bouckaert gave evidence on that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time or have you become aware since then, Mr. Bouckaert, that a number of criminal charges were filed in relation to this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would be happy to hear so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you haven't that information in your possession; is that --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And should evidence be led in this courtroom in relation to this matter, you would not take issue with it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That depends on the credibility of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Bouckaert, for your patience. Your Honour, that would conclude the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no questions for this witness, since my colleague has exhausted topics that I wanted to ask questions about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I begin my redirect examination, the Prosecution would simply like to note for the record that, in its view, the provision of Rule 90(H)(2) has not been followed by my colleague. My colleague has not put to this witness the nature of the case of his client that is in contradiction to the evidence of this witness. Having said that -- and the Prosecution would ask that this be taken into account if there are any arguments raised later on about the credibility of this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Saxon, we don't want to leave that sort of issue in the air. What is it that you say has not been done?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This witness, Your Honour, has not been given an opportunity to respond to a clear message from Defence counsel as to what is the case of the Defence in this case which is in contradiction to the evidence and to the work of this witness, since there were a number of questions, Your Honour, challenging the methods, the results, the writing, the findings of the work this witness, I think this witness, who's been very patient with all of this, should at least have the opportunity to have that position put to him so that he may respond and that opportunity has not been given to him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the -- obviously the Defence does not share the position of Mr. Saxon in relation to this matter. I think it's been quite clear what our position is in relation to this particular witness. We have no reason to doubt the honesty of this witness, and we haven't sought to challenge this matter. What we have challenged, however, and I think the witness himself would be quite aware of that fact, is the reliability of the material which he has obtained, the manner in which the investigation was conducted, the way in which the material was verified, and all of the issues which are relevant to the weight to be given to the evidence of Mr. Bouckaert. If Mr. Saxon's concern is that we haven't put a suggestion to the witness that he had been dishonest in his work, it's certainly not our position. We have absolutely no reason and will make no submissions to that effect, that he had been dishonest in his evidence. I believe that if an issue of concern for Mr. Saxon is the admissibility or otherwise of the report of Mr. Bouckaert, this is an issue that should not be raised as Mr. Saxon just did in front of the witness, but that it should await the discussion once Mr. Bouckaert is gone, about the admissibility of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, as I understand Mr. Saxon, he is saying, well, while you have questioned particular matters, you have not put what it is you say about those matters yourself, what is your own case. You have questioned Mr. Bouckaert in his methods and perhaps some conclusions, but left unsaid and unspecified is what it is that you will wish to put, if anything, directly to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the evidence which we've put to this witness will be put to a number of other witnesses, be it in relation to the status of the civilians, for one, about the circumstances in which the people came to die, about the issue, for example, among other things, of the assertion made by Mr. Bouckaert or by Human Rights Watch, in any case, about the alleged perpetrator having been under the authority of Mr. Boskoski, the issue of the reliability of a number of witnesses who Mr. Bouckaert interviewed and who also appeared in this courtroom as witnesses for the Prosecution, also in relation to the manner in which timing of destruction of houses, about the issue of the nature of the NLA and the legal characterisation of the NLA insofar as it may be relevant to the existence or otherwise of an armed conflict at the time. I believe that we've made those points and a number of others quite clearly through this witness. The issue which is relevant to the credibility of Mr. Bouckaert, in our view, is not whether Mr. Bouckaert did or did not act properly, as he saw it. As I mentioned, we have no reason to believe that Mr. Bouckaert was dishonest in any ways, and we insist again on that point. What we believe, however, is that his investigation, the one man, one week, and we will say also to a large extent one-sided investigation, may not be necessarily be trusted in relation to matter which are not otherwise corroborated by evidence which we have had an opportunity to challenge in this courtroom. One of the issues which we will raise at the time, the report will be sought to be tendered, will be the question of individuals which Mr. Bouckaert interviewed in the course of his investigation and which the Prosecution did not call as witnesses. The situation for us is that we can certainly cross-examine Mr. Bouckaert in relation to his methodology, as we did, to the measures which he took to verify the information, but we are not in a position to cross-examine the witness, himself, or the accuracy of his or her version of events or evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I've got to say, Mr. Mettraux, that what you are there saying seems to me to go much further in respect of a number of these subjects, than anything that was specifically put to the witness. Clearly, it's in your mind, something was in your mind that led you to ask a number of the questions, but it never has come to the point, for example, where you have said to the witness, "I must put to you that it is the case for the accused Mr. Boskoski that the NLA was a terrorist organisation at the time," to allow Mr. Bouckaert an opportunity to comment on that point. You've been testing Mr. Bouckaert on his view that it was not, but you've never gone to the positive side, your own case, if it is your own case, that the NLA was a terrorist organisation. And I think that is the point of the concern and objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if it is the Chamber's view that it could have created an unfairness to Mr. Bouckaert in relation to some of those issues, we would certainly be ready and willing to put those propositions to him. We understood Mr. Bouckaert, and I believe he understood the questions from our questioning, in the sense that this indeed was our position, and if Mr. Bouckaert feels or if the Chamber, rather, feels that this might have created an ambiguity or an unfairness to Mr. Bouckaert, we could certainly put these propositions to him. We believe we have done so in relation to the reliability of the evidence, in relation to the status of the alleged victims, in relation to the houses and the circumstances under which the houses had been damaged, and the other issues which we've pointed out above. If Your Honours wishes us to put the proposition more directly to the witness, we would certainly be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, the Chamber is concerned because the rule referred to by Mr. Saxon is one designed in this adversarial process to ensure that each party cross-examining, and of course it will be the boot on the other foot when it comes to the Prosecution cross-examining, should we reach that point, the concern of the rule is that each party should make clear to witnesses who are contradicting the party's case what it is that the party's case is on material points of difference between the case and the evidence of the witness so that the witness can comment on it. In that way, the Chamber, at the end of the evidence, is not left with a lot of testing questions, but never the final proposition being able to be faced by the witness, and so it's a very important element in the process of coming to final conclusions in a trial. For that reason, the Chamber would certainly take the view that it would be proper for you to be putting your own case about these matters briefly but clearly to the witness to give him an opportunity of directly commenting on those propositions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, following the instructions of the Trial Chamber, I will put a number of propositions to you, and you can indicate whether you agree with the proposition or not. Concerning perhaps the first issue, the issue of the houses in Ljuboten, it is the Defence case, and I'm putting it to you, that a number of houses -- an unidentified number of houses were destroyed not on the 12th of August, not on the 10th or 11th of August, but at later dates in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not our information. We have information that a few houses, one Macedonian house and, according to my notes, one Albanian house, it's possible that there were one or two more, were burned after the events of the 12th of Ljuboten [sic], but certainly not any houses beyond that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also the Defence case that a number of the houses were or might have been destroyed by mortar fire. Would you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not -- actually, there is one house marked on my map which was destroyed by mortar fire. The majority of the homes, as indicated on my map, were destroyed by being set on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also the Defence case that on the 10th, 11th and 12th of August, members of the NLA were in the village of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: We have no indication to suggest that any NLA members were in the direct area that was targeted during the August 12th operation and that there was any return fire from the NLA or other armed persons during the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also the Defence case that a number of mortars fired on the village of Ljuboten came from the position of the NLA. Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have no information as to that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also the Defence case that some of the victims or alleged victims who you regarded as civilians and regarded as having been murdered were or might, in fact, have been members of the NLA or civilians taking part in hostilities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to all of the information available to us, all of those persons who were killed were not members of the NLA, and they were not civilians taking part in hostilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also the Defence case that in 2001, there was -- at no time in 2001, there was no armed conflict in the Republic of Macedonia. Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there's a double negative. Are you saying that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it for you, Mr. Bouckaert. It is the Defence position that in the year 2001, there was no armed conflict in Macedonia. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. According to our analysis, the conflict in Macedonia amounted to an internal armed conflict, as defined under Common Article 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also the Defence position that the NLA was a terrorist group and that its actions against the Macedonian authority were terrorist attacks. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also the position of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski that contrary to your allegation, Mr. Boskoski -- or the alleged perpetrators were not under his authority or under his command. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The abuses in Ljuboten were carried out by Ministry of Interior troops under the authority of Mr. Boskoski, and he was personally present in Ljuboten on August 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also the position of the Defence that your investigation and the fruit of this investigation is unreliable. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think our investigation was -- no, I do not agree. Our investigation was reliable. It was based on detailed interviews and analysis of a lot of information available to us, and I have no information to suggest that any of the information in our report is inaccurate or unreliable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also our case that you failed to verify many of the allegations contained in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also the position of the Defence that Mr. Boskoski and the Macedonian authorities took a great number of steps to investigate the events of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is also the Defence position that your conclusion in that respect are based on the fact that you did not possess that information and made no request to obtain that information. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: We have no information available to Human Rights Watch and do not know of any information in the public sphere to suggest that a credible investigation took place into the events of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bouckaert. Your Honour, I think -- I hope we have complied with the Rule 90(H)(2).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber can't form a final view on that, but it is at your risk if you don't, you realise, under the rule. There will be consequences later, so it must be for you to give conscientious attention to compliance with the Rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps what we could propose is if the Chamber were minded to give us a short break of five minutes, we could very quickly go through the record to see whether there's another matter which, in fairness to Mr. Bouckaert, we should put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That may be a safe precaution, Mr. Mettraux, and it's a precaution that I would also address to Mr. Apostolski, because the issue arises for both accused, and matters that you have raised may not entirely cover issues that the Defence of Mr. Tarculovski would want to raise. So combining all those things and the progress of the clock, what the Chamber might do is to have the first break now, resume at 10 to 4.00, and then allow, if necessary, time for those further matters to be put by Mr. Mettraux and Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, are there any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, and we're grateful for the time given to us to look through the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, I'm sorry to delay the matter. There is a number of other propositions that we would like to put to you in manner that we followed prior to the break. The first proposition is that the goal or purpose was not as you concluded, with a view to inflict any sort revenge, but it was a search operation against terrorists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I should put it again to you, it was not motivated by any intention to exert revenge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the interpreters ask you again to slow down for the transcript, for us, and the audience listening to us, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The President of the Republic of Macedonia was the legitimate and constitutionally-empowered authority to order such operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: The -- such operations could also be initiated from within the Ministry of Interior, so no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of the victims mentioned in your report, and I am speaking of the persons who you said were murdered on that day, were or might have been killed by members of the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the case of the victims of shelling, yes. In the case of the people who were shot dead or later died in custody, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Houses which were targeted in the course of the activities on the 10th, 11th, and 12th of August were or might have been legitimate military targets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: We found no evidence to suggest that any of the houses targeted were legitimate military targets. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The NLA or members of the NLA would at times dress in civilian clothes to carry out operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never saw NLA members in civilian clothes at the times I met them, and that I am not aware of any incident in which they were in civilian clothes during military operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm putting to you that the dead or the deceased in the village of Ljuboten were killed or might have been killed as a result of combat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: None of the dead or deceased were executed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no indiscriminate fire at homes of civilians; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of the people involved in the operation were neither members or de jure members of either the army or the Ministry of Interior; is that correct or not, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is possible that other armed civilians were involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A general assertion about Mr. Boskoski's acceptance of crimes committed by members of the police is wrong and unsubstantiated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no indiscriminate attack on civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Our research concludes that there were either deliberate or indiscriminate attacks on civilians at Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the Defence case that none of the five alleged victims of murders reported in your report were killed in the manner stated by you in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Is it correct that that is the Defence case?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting to you that your conclusion in relation to the manner in which these five persons were killed is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I stand by the findings of my report and believe that they are correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And even though we've indicated that you've acted honestly, your judgement has been distorted by your wish to see Mr. Boskoski being convicted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, and I think my record of investigating the crimes of NLA members clearly shows that I had a balanced approach in my investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this bias or this prejudice against Mr. Boskoski has affected the reliability of the findings and explain the facts that you sought or that you failed to seek to verify the information concerning his presence and his actions on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your observations and finding as regard the body of Mr. Qaili are wrong. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is the Defence case that your finding as regard the involvement of de jure police officers, reservists, or active police officers in beatings are wrong, or unreliable, or not sufficiently verified. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12th of August, Mr. Boskoski was not in Ljuboten but in Ljubanci. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was not in either Ljubanci or Ljuboten on that day during the entire operation, as recorded in your report, but only for a much shorter period of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wish to correct you. Our report does not state that he was present during the entire operation. It states that the Macedonian national media claimed that he was present during the entire operation. Later on in the same paragraph, we state that Mr. Boskoski acknowledged that he was in Ljuboten, but claims that he arrived at about 4.00 p.m. Our report only concludes that Mr. Boskoski was present at Ljuboten sometime during the day of August 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is the Defence case that there were NLA defensive positions and mortar positions of the NLA in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not to our knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your information has recounted to the Prosecution in relation to the events of Bitola to the matter of the paramilitary 2000, also known as The Lions, and other incidents which you were asked about and reported about is incomplete or wrong; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your conclusions generally in your reports are unreliable, unverified, or incomplete. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You failed to take even the most basic steps to verify the accuracy, the reliability, or the truth of many of the accounts which were given to you by the villagers in Ljuboten; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your views about The Lions as you explained to the Prosecution but also in your statement is wrong, uninformed and without any evidential basis. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as regard the allegations which you raised against Mr. Boskoski in your report and in other letters, you failed to comply with the most basic rules of fairness and justice; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we have covered the issues which we wish to put directly to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I support all the issues stressed by my colleague Mettraux, and I wish to highlight just a few more issues as follows:

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bouckaert, is it correct that the action of the Macedonian security forces in the village of Ljuboten was legitimate?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Our conclusion is that it was either an indiscriminate or a deliberate attack on civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At the same time, it was necessary for the Macedonian security forces to intervene in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The action was a joint action with the Macedonian military forces, is that correct, of the army and of the police?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to our information, the role of the army was limited to shelling of the village, and we have no information to suggest that they took any role in the ground operation on the 12th. I should also point out that at least some of the soldiers initially objected about becoming involved in the action on Ljuboten, as is clear from the evidence presented by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was still a joint operation, as I understood from your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would not characterise it as a joint operation, especially not the operation which involved the crimes committed on August 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your report is based on uncorroborated information received only from ethnic Albanians?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was prepared without interviewing a single Macedonian inhabitant of the village of Ljuboten; although there are Macedonians who live in that village?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Macedonian population of the village was not present during my visit to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You've mentioned that a house of a Macedonian was arsonned. Did you take a statement from that Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you try to interview him?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were unable to locate him. We did not have any contact information for him. We did include the information about the burning of his home in our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you had data on him, you knew his name and last name; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Actually, we only knew his first name, Zlatko.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Simply as a matter of fairness to the Prosecution before they start with the re-examination, we would like to indicate at this stage that Mr. Bouckaert is being called not as an expert but as a fact witness, and, that as such, we will make submissions in relation to the evidence which is given distinguishing between the factual evidence which is given and the opinions which he has given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the Chamber mention, for all counsel but particularly Defence counsel at this stage, that the process that has just been followed is the sort of process that is to be expected with compliance with the rules, where a witness deals with a range of facts as extensive as this witness. Of course, most witnesses will be dealing with a much more limited range of facts so that the point of the Defence case that might contradict with that witness will be much more limited and confined. But a witness such as this, the process we have just followed is appropriate. Now, Mr. Saxon, we come to you again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, a few minutes ago it was put to you by my colleague that your judgement is distorted by your need to see or your desire to see certain persons prosecuted. You mentioned earlier in your testimony that you've been doing some work recently in the Central African Republic. Are you aware that the International Criminal Court is also working or has opened an investigation into the Central African Republic?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that fact. Their investigation currently focuses on the events of 2002-2003, but they are monitoring the current situation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Have you provided any assistance or advice to the members of the International Criminal Court who are working on these issues?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have informed them, as well as the Darfur team, of my work on these two war zones and have offered any assistance they would like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Has anyone in that capacity ever questioned your judgement or suggested that it was distorted by a need to see people prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I spent half of my time working on -- under some of the most difficult conditions because I believe in accountability in general. Working in war zones, getting malaria, getting sick, because I believe in this work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But I need you to answer my question, sir.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Well, certainly, whenever I testify or whenever we accuse anybody of or any government of violating human rights or the laws of war, we get accused of a lack of judgement or a bias.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But my question -- I'm sorry, my question wasn't clear enough. Relating to your work with members at the International Criminal Court, have any of the staff there, working on these issues, questioned your judgement?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe yesterday, at page 3186 of the transcript, you commented that: "People were beaten to death in the streets of Skopje by police officers in front of large crowds," and that such an event, if unanswered by the Minister of the Interior, would qualify as openly tolerating police abuse. Can we see what is Exhibit P361, please. If we could increase the size of that, please. Can we -- we need to look at the bottom of this page. Mr. Bouckaert, this is a report written in August of 2001 describing an event on the 13th of August of 2001. In the paragraph beginning: "On Monday, August 13th ...," it refers to police officers beating, in the last sentence, "four men in the street in front of the hospital." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Those were ethnic Albanian men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, on the day after the events in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The following paragraph, it says: "The men were then taken onto the hospital grounds and beaten continuously for several hours with heavy metal cables, baseball bats, police truncheons, and gun butts amidst jeering from the civilian crowd that had gathered." Then it said, "The four men were taken to the Bako 1 police station, they were subjected to more beatings." And at the end of the paragraph, it says: "One of the men, 29-year-old Nazmi Aliu, father of a six-year-old and a two-year-old, died that --" Can we go to the next page, please. " ... Died that day at the hospital from the injuries he received from the police beatings." And then it goes on to talk about the researchers who interviewed two of the surviving men. Were you one of those researchers?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is this the incident that you were referring to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was the second incident in which people had been beaten in front of this very public hospital, but it is the incident in which a person was beaten to death, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At page 3502 of the transcript, you were asked by my colleague why you did not seek an official response from the Macedonian government or Mr. Boskoski regarding the events in Ljuboten prior to the publication of your report. And you say at page 3502: "I feel that the position of --" or: "We felt that the position of Mr. Boskoski and the government was reflected in our report based on public statements made by him and the government." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to show, please, what is a video clip, with the assistance of Ms. Walpita. It is 65 ter 305. It comes from ERN V000-5202, and it's a video of a press conference which is also discussed in the testimony of Mr. Bouckaert at page 3192 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, you heard Mr. Boskoski refer -- use the term "terrorist," I think, three times in the clip that I just showed you, one when he said that "serves to prove that a massacre did not occur in the village of Ljuboten," and that there was no killing of civilians but of a terrorist-extremist group, and then more recently when Mr. Boskoski explained that the residents of village of Ljuboten buried these five terrorists, and all that remains now is to establish whether they were from Ljuboten, itself, or whether these terrorists were also imported. Was this one of the public statements of Minister Boskoski that, in your mind, before you wrote the report, reflected his position and the position of his government?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and it's mentioned in our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would seek to tender this video clip, which is from 001655 to 002256, 65 ter number 305.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply to indicate, Your Honour, that the passage in question has been put, it's on the transcript, and the proposition which Mr. Saxon wanted to put has been clearly answered by the witness. We don't see, at this stage, a need to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Anything, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, simply that questions were put to this witness on cross-examination as to what material he used to make his professional judgements in the writing of the report, and one of the materials that he used were television news broadcasts, including this one. So it is the video material itself that is actually the most relevant evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be admitted, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P362, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we move into private session, please, briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, at page 3056 and 3057 of the transcript, you mentioned that you had discussions with Mr. Henry Bolton and Ms. Sandra Mitchell about the events that occurred in Ljuboten village, and these two persons were part of the OSCE mission in Macedonia at the time. Can you help us, please: Why did you have discussions with these two individuals and not other members of the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: As I think our report makes clear, we had some basic disagreements with the OSCE about their monitoring of the conflict and the reporting they were doing. For example, we felt that, although, we knew they had knowledge of the widespread police abuse that was taking place at the time, we knew this because many of the people that we interviewed, who had been abused in police custody, mentioned the fact to us that they had also been interviewed by OSCE monitors. They did not speak publicly about these abuses. So I would say that we had less than cordial relations at the time, and we were concerned about the impartiality of the OSCE and these two people, some -- I mean, Sandra had also worked on Kosovo. They were people that we felt comfortable talking to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You're referring now to Mr. Bolton and Ms. Mitchell?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you said in the record, "They did not speak publicly about these abuses" --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: That would be the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. At page 3159 of the transcript, you refer to fierce discussions within the OSCE after the events in Ljuboten between Mr. Bolton and a person you refer to as the Human Dimension Officer about the reliability of reports from other international observers about the presence of armed ethnic Albanians in Ljuboten and exchanges of fire on the 12th of August, 2001. How do you know about these discussions?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know if I said that they were specifically between the Human Dimensions Officers and Mr. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were aware that there were basic disagreements within the OSCE about the reliability of some of those reports and also about some of the allegations that were made in the OSCE report of August 16th, I believe, which put forth alternative theories, that some of the people killed could have been killed by ethnic Albanian elements, because we -- there were people within the OSCE who felt that there was no basis to make those kind of statements, yes. So it's based on our informal contacts within the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At pages 3074 to 3075, and again on page 3078, there are discussions between you and my colleague about sections of the report that you wrote about the events in Ljuboten which describe or refer to the responsibility of the Macedonian security forces and the role of the then Minister of the Interior, Mr. Boskoski, and during that portion of your testimony you were asked questions about your reliance on a video news broadcast from Macedonian State Television on the evening of 12th August. Do you recall some of that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask Ms. Walpita's assistance again, please, to show you that broadcast, Mr. Bouckaert, from Macedonian Television. It's from 65 ter number 305, ERN V000-5202, and this clip will go from 00.11.52 to 00.15.14.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel switch off one of his microphones? It creates noise for us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if Your Honours wear your earphones, you'd be hearing gunfire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are able to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, do you recognise this video material as the Macedonian State Television broadcast that you used as a reference in your report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and we had a still from that broadcast as a photograph in our report also.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender the clip that I just showed, the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. That was my mistake, and I think I know what the objection is. At this time, the Prosecution would simply seek to mark this clip for identification, because the news -- the news reporter whose voice we heard will be testifying later on in this case. That was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P363, MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like, Mr. Bouckaert, please, if you could turn your mind to a different topic now.
